chunks: Ghayb of al-Tusi: Via his chain to Abdallah b. Ja'far who said:

A Tawqi [signed rescript] came out to the Shaykh Abi Ja'far Muhammad b. Uthman b. Sai'd al-Amri (may God sanctify his soul) condoling him for the death of his father (may God be pleased with him). In it was written: … May Allah amplify your reward and beautify your mourning. We grieve just as you grieve. It has left you bereft just as it has left us bereft. May Allah delight him after his return. One aspect of the perfect felicity he attained is that Allah the Exalted granted him a son like you, who succeeds him after his departure, stands in his place as per his command, and supplicates for mercy for him. I say 'All praise belongs to Allah' for the souls are comforted due to the position you have assumed and because of what Allah Mighty and Majestic has bestowed in you and with you. May Allah support and strengthen you. May He aid you and facilitate you. May He be a Guardian over you, a Protector, a Guide and Sufficient for you.

key_terms.التَّوْقِيع: Signed rescript or decree from the Imam
key_terms.رَزِزْتُ وَرَزِينَا: We grieved and we were bereaved

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam's rescript say about the relationship between the father's death and the son's succession?
ai.summary: This Tawqi from the Imam to Muhammad b. Uthman al-Amri highlights the concept of *khalifah* (successorship), where the son is praised not merely as a relative but as the one who continues the father's spiritual and administrative authority. The text emphasizes the divine wisdom in granting a worthy successor, framing the loss as a transition of trust rather than a complete severance, a key theme in Shia understanding of Imamate and scholarly lineage. It serves as a model for how the Imamate validates the status of the *Bab* (Gate) or chief deputy through personal correspondence.

en.ammaar-muslim: 2. [2/247] Ghayba of al-Tusi: Via his chain to Abdallah b. Ja’far who said:

A Tawqi [signed rescript] came out to the Shaykh Abi Ja’far Muhammad b. Uthman b. Sai’d al-Amri قدس الله روحه condoling him for the death of his father رضي الله تعالى عنه. In it was written: … May Allah amplify your reward and beautify your mourning. We grieve just as you grieve. It [his death] has left you bereft just as it has left us bereft. May Allah delight him after his return [to Him]. One aspect of the perfect felicity [he attained] is that Allah the Exalted granted him a son like you, who succeeds him after his departure, stands in his place as per his command, and supplicates for mercy for him. I say ‘All praise belongs to Allah’ for the souls are comforted due to the position you have assumed [after him] and because of what Allah Mighty and Majestic has bestowed in you and with you. May Allah support and strengthen you. May He aid you and facilitate you. May He be a Guardian over you, a Protector, a Guide and Sufficient [for you].
